title: Personal Credit Cards: Fixed Amount of the Closing Automatic Payment
content:
This page brings together how the fixed sum of a Personal Credit Cards closing automatic payment is arrived at, and when it is nil.

## Rule

- Where the ledger shows the card still owing and the cardholder keeps a PCB checking account in active status, the fixed sum is the balance owed as limited by the last statement balance, rounded half-up to the cent.
- Where the ledger shows nothing owed, or a credit, a closing automatic payment has nothing to do and the sum is 0.00 USD.
- Where the cardholder keeps no PCB checking account in active status, there is nowhere for a closing automatic payment to draw from, and the sum is 0.00 USD.

The rounding to the cent is applied a single time, to the final figure, never to the intermediate totals.

## Truth table

| Balance owed above zero | Active PCB checking held | Fixed sum |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the lower of the balance owed and the last statement balance, rounded half-up once |
| yes | no | 0.00 USD |
| no | yes | 0.00 USD |
| no | no | 0.00 USD |

## Worked case (hypothetical)

A card owes 1453.40 USD by its ledger, its last statement showed 1390.12 USD, and the cardholder keeps an active checking account: the fixed sum is 1390.12 USD. The same card with a ledger figure of minus 12.00 USD, a credit, needs no closing automatic payment.
